_provenance.what: The Kālasetu Siddhānta long-span engine's fitted numbers: corrections on the Later Sūrya Siddhānta's own mean-motion count, the orbit of each body, and the measured amplitudes of the further terms.
_provenance.target: source/data/kalasetu-reference.json: JPL DE422 over about 3000 BCE – 3000 CE; beyond it, the Sun and planets from a numerical integration started from DE422's own states (source/tools/nbody.mjs), and the Moon and true node from JPL DE431 over the whole span. Apparent geocentric, true ecliptic of date, Samanvaya–Ecliptic frame; the mean node against the published polynomial.
_provenance.span: 5000 BCE – 3600 CE (astronomical years -4999 to 3600), 3,600 instants, hashed half held back. Every residual below is the held-back half's unless labelled fit. Bias is the mean signed residual (engine − reference).
_provenance.notTheText: Not the Sūrya Siddhānta's answer. The time-count is the text's; the geometry is not — see the header of kalasetu-engine.js for exactly what was added and from where.
_provenance.limits: Agreement with the reference above. Before 3000 BCE the planets rest on the integration (checked against DE422 across DE422's own 6000 years) and the Moon on JPL DE431's integrated lunar orbit (Folkner et al. 2014), an independent reference across the whole span; ΔT is uncertain by hours at 5000 BCE and by most of a day at 13000 BCE.
_provenance.units: residuals in arcminutes of longitude (latitude where given)

moon.on: JPL DE431 at every instant of this set
moon.note: fitted on JPL DE431's Moon (an integrated lunar orbit with tidal dissipation, 13201 BCE – 17191 CE) at this set's own instants; its residuals are against DE431, an independent reference, across the whole span

integrator_check.note: heliocentric direction, arcseconds, integration minus DE422 after starting from DE422 at 3000 BCE

moon_correction.note: arcseconds; T in Julian centuries from J2000; residual rms is the scatter left on the overlap

modern_vs_reference.note: the modern engine (astronomy-engine) minus this reference, arcminutes, on the verification draw

Rāhu (true).against: the osculating node of JPL DE431's Moon
